title: ELV or DHR: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
author: Na
description: In a comparison of two Medical Services stocks, Elevance Health (ELV) emerges as the superior value option over Danaher (DHR). ELV holds a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a Value grade of A, featuring a forward P/E of 15.70 and PEG ratio of 2.22. DHR has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a Value grade of D, with a forward P/E of 23.84 and PEG ratio of 2.53. Based on valuation metrics and earnings outlook, ELV is positioned as the better value investment.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: ELV has a stronger Zacks Rank (#2 Buy vs #3 Hold), superior Value grade (A vs D), lower forward P/E ratio (15.70 vs 23.84), lower PEG ratio (2.22 vs 2.53), and lower P/B ratio (2.04 vs 2.72), indicating better valuation and stronger earnings improvement outlook.

DHR is rated as a Hold with a D Value grade, indicating it is less attractive as a value investment compared to ELV. While not negatively positioned, it shows weaker valuation metrics and a less favorable earnings outlook.

title: Here's How CVS' Health Services Arm Is Positioned for Long-Term Growth
author: Zacks.Com
description: CVS Health's Health Services segment demonstrated strong Q2 2026 performance with revenues rising 11.5% to $51.8B and adjusted operating income climbing 10%. Health Care Delivery revenues jumped nearly 23% driven by Oak Street Health, while Pharmacy Services benefited from favorable drug mix and strong new sales of $6B. The company maintained its full-year 2026 outlook despite 340B program adjustments.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 2026 results with 11.5% revenue growth and 10% operating income growth. Health Care Delivery segment surged 23%, new pharmacy sales exceeded historical averages at $6B, and the company maintained full-year guidance. Stock has outperformed industry peers with 30.1% gains over the past year and trades at attractive valuation metrics.

Optum health services business continues as a key growth engine with 11.6% revenue growth in 2024 and 7% in 2025. OptumHealth's integrated value-based care model and AI-enabled technologies support longer-term growth and margin expansion prospects.

Carelon healthcare services brand showed 7.1% revenue growth to $37.2B in H1 2026. Strategic expansion of integrated capabilities across pharmacy, behavioral health, and value-based care solutions positions the company for revenue diversification and future growth.

title: Can Centene's Medicare Advantage Strategy Unlock Better Margins?
author: Na
description: Centene Corporation is simplifying its Medicare Advantage footprint and emphasizing dual-eligible members to improve portfolio quality and margins. The company's Medicare segment health benefits ratio improved to 89.5% in Q2 2026, with MA moving closer to breakeven. For 2027, Centene aims to achieve breakeven or better MA results through medical-cost control, Stars execution, and SG&A management.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Centene shows improving fundamentals with health benefits ratio improvement from 90.9% to 89.5%, MA approaching breakeven, strong YTD stock performance (+59%), attractive valuation (P/E 12.57 vs industry 15.80), and Zacks Rank #1 Strong Buy rating with consensus 2026 earnings growth of 135.1%.

UnitedHealth Group demonstrated margin recovery progress with medical care ratio improving from 89.4% to 86.7% in Q2 2026, showing effective management of elevated medical costs through repricing and benefit redesign strategies.

Elevance Health is taking a selective approach to Medicare Advantage with membership declines, facing pressure from higher medical costs, but showing potential for future profitability through pricing discipline and Carelon-led cost management initiatives.

title: UnitedHealth Stock Rises 39% in 6 Months: Should Investors Still Buy?
author: Zacks.Com
description: UnitedHealth (UNH) has surged 38.8% over six months as medical-cost pressures ease and confidence improves. The company's medical care ratio fell to 85.3%, medical costs declined 2%, and 2026 EPS estimates rose 21.2% to $19.82. Despite the rally, UNH trades below its five-year median valuation and analyst price targets, suggesting further upside potential. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

Stock rated Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with 20.5% upside to analyst targets.

title: Should You Invest in the iShares U.S. Healthcare Providers ETF (IHF)?
author: Zacks.Com
description: The iShares U.S. Healthcare Providers ETF (IHF) is a passively managed fund launched in 2006 that tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Select HealthCare Providers Index. With $1.25 billion in assets, a competitive 0.37% expense ratio, and a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), it offers diversified exposure to healthcare providers. Year-to-date performance is up 20.18%, with a medium risk profile (beta of 0.72). Top holdings include UnitedHealth Group (20.61%), CVS Health, and Elevance Health.
